note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: 3-day history of diarrhea; no recent travel, no unusual food intake reported.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Began ~3 days ago; currently 4–5 loose/watery bowel motions per day; one episode of vomiting; mild abdominal pain; possible low-grade fever; decreased appetite but able to maintain oral intake.
- ENT symptoms: Denies throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change/hoarseness, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, ear pain/hearing changes, neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: Occasional self-limited diarrhea in past after certain foods or travel; no prior hospital care, epinephrine, or ED visits for similar.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergies: None reported.  
  • Medications: “Lexapro” (patient states this is an asthma inhaler; dose/route/frequency not documented) – conflict noted as Lexapro is typically escitalopram.
- Social context: Patient alone during video consult; appears able to follow advice.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution: None reported or visualized.
- Airway/breathing: No stridor, dyspnea, or respiratory distress reported.
- Mental status: Alert; no dizziness or syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person: None mentioned.

Assessment:
- Self-limited gastroenteritis/diarrhea; no current features of dehydration or red-flag symptoms.
- No ENT involvement identified.
- Medication identity conflict: Patient describes “Lexapro” as yellow asthma inhaler; requires clarification.

Plan:
- Dietary advice: Soft/bland diet (crackers, toast, mashed vegetables); avoid dairy, meat, fish, eggs until ≥48 h diarrhea-free; consider yogurt for probiotics.
- Hydration: Drink plenty of fluids; use OTC oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte) as needed.
- Escalation criteria/red flags: Seek medical attention if ≥6–8 diarrheal stools/day, presence of blood or mucus, persistent diarrhea >1 week, signs of dehydration (dry mouth, dizziness), uncontrolled vomiting, high fever, or abdominal pain worsening.
- Follow-up: Contact service again or attend hospital if above criteria met; clinician will document advice in app for patient review.
- Medication clarification: Patient to confirm inhaler name and regimen with primary care provider/asthma service.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing elements: Vitals, physical examination, detailed medication list with doses, formal allergy confirmation, past anaphylaxis/ENT history, availability of rescue asthma inhaler.  
• Internal conflicts: Patient calls “Lexapro” an asthma inhaler (conflict with known drug name).  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor conversational overlaps but clinically adequate.
